Is a government's first duty to its citizens - or all of its inhabitants regardless of citizenship?

This might be unpopular with reactionaries with poor reading comprehension, but since a nation has fixed geographical borders and a constantly changing population, its first duty is to whoever might happen to be within those geographical borders, regardless of citizenship.

That said, the range of its duties to citizens and non-citizens should be different - that is, in fact, the exact point of citizenship - to differentiate between those who have entered into an official arrangement with the government and those who just happen to be within its borders. It absolutely should be the case that those who have made the commitment to citizenship are rewarded for having done so. Still though, its responsibility is to all who are within its borders, since those borders are what really define the nation.

A few voaters helped me fine-tune some ideas on how Voat could mitigate mod access for newly added mods in a way that wouldn't severely impact existing and trustworthy mods: https://voat.co/v/ideasforvoat/comments/1107437/5507470

The gist of it is this:

  • L1 - full permissions to delete posts, add/remove mods, full subverse settings access
  • L2 - no deletion of content older than their mod status, ability to add/remove L3 mods, full subverse settings access
  • L3 - no deletion of content older than their mod status, no ability to add/remove mods, no subverse settings access

L2s of system subs who have been around a while have pretty much would have all the permissions they currently have, plus the ability to add L3s. On non-system subs, the L1 would retain control of other mods, but any L3s that those mods add won't be able to go back and remove posts that predate their mod status, nor will they be able to modify sub settings or add/remove mods themselves. L2s wouldn't be able to add or remove other L2s, and would still need the L1 to approve those changes.
